A gem in the heart of the medina, Essaraya.
Dec 2025 • Friends
We had a very pleasant evening at Essaraya. The place is magnificent, with an authentic and warm atmosphere in the heart of the medina. The decoration and atmosphere make the experience truly special.

The dishes were flavorful and well presented, with a wonderful discovery of traditional Tunisian cuisine. The service was attentive and professional, while remaining natural and welcoming.

The value for money is fair considering the setting and the experience offered. The waiting time was reasonable and the overall atmosphere was very pleasant, especially with the traditional music in the background.

A beautiful place to discover for a good time in a typical setting of Tunis.

Incredible experience
Feb 2026 • Family
I had such a wonderful evening at Essaraya Restaurant with my family. From the moment we arrived, we were greeted with smiles and a welcoming atmosphere. The staff were attentive without being overbearing, the maître enthusiastically shared shared stories about the medina and the History of Tunisia.

We ended up trying several dishes, Chorba, Couscous and salads, every single one was very good. The flavors were rich, the portions were generous, and the presentation was beautiful. We especially loved sharing the mezze platters—it gave us a chance to taste a little bit of everything. The desserts were a real highlight too; even my kids were excited to dig in, which says a lot!

The atmosphere of the restaurant is warm and cozy, but still lively with the live musicien playing, it really felt like a special night out. It’s the kind of place where you can relax, enjoy your meal, and actually spend quality time with family. We left feeling full, happy, and completely satisfied with the experience.

Essaraya is definitely a place we’ll be returning to. If you’re looking for great food, friendly service, a welcoming vibe, and tells of History, this is the spot. Highly recommended!

Restaurants in aristocratic residences

The combination of harissa and bread was delicious, though. There are no alcoholic beverages here. That is one of the unfortunate things.

Good, but could be better
Oct 2024 • Couples
We tried Essaraya for dinner on our hotel's recommendation, and like some others have noted we had to ask for assistance to find it. When we arrived at 18:30 we were the only diners, and even after an hour the main room was only one quarter full. While we waited we admired the restaurant's interior, which is quite decorative and photo-worthy. A musician played an Oud (a stringed, lute-like instrument). Our waiter was multilingual and provided us with an English menu, so it is likely that this place fills up with international tours over lunch. The shortfall of our evening was the food. Although the complementary mezze of baba ghanoush, harissa, and a carrot salad were nice, the mains of lamb couscous and stuffed veal were underflavoured and a bit dry.

A quiet pleasant evening
Feb 2024 • Couples
On our short break in Tunis we went for a meal to Essaraya. Found it a little difficult to get there because on the unfamiliarity of the area. It was in a quiet street (everyone closes by 6pm). The atmosphere was lovely, there was live singer. The deco was traditional (see the short clip). We didn't have a starter and had a main meal. I opted for couscous with lamb and kindly they gave my husband chicken couscous. Food was 7/10. Waiters were attentive. 
It was kind when we left there was security to asscort us from the restaurant out of the higgedy pigguldy road into the street.
